# UI Hub

> Curated, multilingual directory of 2391 public UI resources (component libraries, component style demos, effects, design systems, design skills for AI agents) plus original blog analysis of AI design techniques. Data updated 2026-10-15 04:35 UTC.

Use the JSON endpoints, not the SPA, when acting as an agent. Every entry links to its original site; licenses belong to the original authors.

## Design encyclopedia (query this first)
- [Encyclopedia](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/kb/): skills (full SKILL.md where licensed), design specs (spacing, typography, colour, motion, accessibility, dark mode, mobile), house style & lessons, blog notes
- [KB JSON](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/api/kb.json): every entry with type, tags, url, raw .md URL and full markdown
- [Search index](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/api/search-index.json): kb entries + all resources/components, fields t,k,u,r,d,g
- Raw entry pattern: https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/kb/<type>/<slug>.md  (type = skill | spec | note), e.g. https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/kb/spec/motion.md, https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/kb/skill/taste-skill.md
- [Context bundle](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/context-bundle.md): AGENTS.md + all specs + house style + skills index in one file

## Machine-readable
- [Resources JSON](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/api/resources.json): all items with type, ct (component kind), vs (visual style), pricing, url
- [Skills JSON](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/api/skills.json): design + engineering agent skills and the recommended workflow
- [Agent guide](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/agents/): how to search, pick, copy and verify
- [AGENTS.md](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/AGENTS.md)
- [Full text for LLMs](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/llms-full.txt)

## Blog
- [Blog RSS feed](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/rss.xml) · [Blog JSON](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/api/blog.json)
- [AI-assisted UI design: a workflow that keeps taste in the loop](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/ai-assisted-ui-design-workflow/): Generators are fast but average. Split the job: humans set direction and constraints, AI explores variants, humans curate and polish.
- [Prompting for UI: write specs, not wishes](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/prompts-for-ui/): "Modern and clean" means nothing to a model. Name layout, tokens, states, content and what to avoid.
- [Design-to-code with AI: map to your components, not to pixels](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/design-to-code-with-ai/): Pixel-perfect export creates throwaway code. Give the agent your component registry and tokens via MCP so output reuses what you already ship.
- [Teaching agents taste: how design skills de-slop AI interfaces](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/taste-and-skills-for-agents/): Skills like frontend-design, taste-skill and impeccable package opinions as files agents load on demand. Here is how to combine them.
- [Component composition: why headless + copy-paste won](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/component-composition/): Radix behaviour, your styles, code you own. Compound components keep APIs small and make AI edits safer.
- [Motion that feels right: purpose, duration, easing, restraint](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/motion-that-feels-right/): Most UI motion should be under 300ms, ease-out, and skipped for frequent actions. Spectacle belongs on marketing pages, not in tools.
- [Dark mode done right: tokens, elevation and contrast](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/dark-mode-done-right/): Dark mode is a second palette, not an inverted one. Use semantic tokens, lighter surfaces for elevation, and desaturated accents.
- [Accessibility in AI-generated UI: the checks models skip](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/accessibility-in-ai-generated-ui/): Generated UIs look fine and fail keyboards and screen readers. Start from accessible primitives, then audit against WCAG 2.2.
- [v0 in practice: from a prompt to shadcn code you can keep](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/v0-prompt-to-shadcn/): v0 is strongest when you treat it as a shadcn/Tailwind code generator, not a design oracle. Brief it like an engineer, then pull the code into your repo.
- [Lovable and Bolt: when prompt-to-UI becomes prompt-to-app](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/lovable-bolt-prompt-to-app/): Both tools build whole apps, so design quality now competes with data, auth and deploys for attention. How to keep the look from being an afterthought.
- [Figma Make and the Figma agent: AI moves onto the canvas](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/figma-make-and-figma-agent/): Figma Make turns prompts into working prototypes; the Figma agent, generally available since 6 Oct 2026, reads team guideline files. Why the guideline file matters most.
- [MagicOS: Magic Patterns bets on an infinite canvas of AI threads](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/magic-patterns-magicos/): Launched 13 Oct 2026: one coordinator chat spawns parallel design threads on a shared canvas. What it fixes (lost context) and when a single design is still better.
- [Prompt-to-UI tools compared: v0, Lovable, Bolt, Figma Make, Magic Patterns](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/prompt-to-ui-tools-compared/): Not a leaderboard: a decision guide by what you are shipping, where the output lives, and how much design control you need.
- [Aceternity UI deep dive: spectacle, used sparingly](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/aceternity-ui-deep-dive/): Copy-paste React + Tailwind + Motion effects that made the "fancy" landing look popular. Which pieces carry a page and which turn it into a demo reel.
- [Magic UI deep dive: animated components that install like shadcn](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/magic-ui-deep-dive/): An open-source (MIT) set of motion components distributed through the shadcn registry. Best picks for SaaS pages and how to keep them accessible.
- [Cult UI deep dive: tactile components with personality](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/cult-ui-deep-dive/): shadcn-compatible components that feel physical: dynamic islands, textured buttons, expandable cards. How to borrow personality without breaking consistency.
- [shadcn blocks and registries: page sections as source code](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/shadcn-blocks-deep-dive/): Blocks (dashboards, sidebars, login pages) install with one CLI command, and any team can publish its own registry. Why this is the best substrate for AI agents.
- [Typography for AI-generated UI: the fastest way to look less generic](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/typography-for-ai-generated-ui/): Generators default to one sans at three sizes. A type scale, a second typeface, tighter tracking on display sizes and real line lengths fix most of it.
- [OKLCH colour systems: palettes that survive dark mode](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/oklch-color-and-dark-mode/): OKLCH keeps perceived lightness consistent across hues, so you can generate scales and dark themes by math instead of eyeballing. Tailwind v4 uses it by default.
- [Landing page teardown: what Linear and Vercel get right](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/landing-page-teardown-linear-vercel/): Two widely copied developer-tool homepages, read as a list of decisions: one message, product as hero image, dark restraint, and proof placed right after the promise.
- [Dashboard patterns that hold up: from KPI strip to drill-down table](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/dashboard-design-patterns/): AI tools love to generate twelve charts. Good dashboards answer three questions in order: is it OK, what changed, why. A layout and a component list for each.
- [Design tokens for agents: the file that makes AI output on-brand](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/design-tokens-for-agents/): A machine-readable token file (the W3C DTCG format) plus a short usage note beats any adjective in a prompt. Structure, naming, and how to hand it to an agent.
- [Design skills for Claude and Cursor: SKILL.md, rules and AGENTS.md](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/claude-cursor-design-skills/): Three file formats, one idea: durable instructions an agent loads when relevant. How to write a design skill that changes output, with a template.
- [Weekly roundup, 14 Oct 2026: guideline files go mainstream](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/weekly-roundup-2026-w42/): Figma agent GA with team guidelines, Lovable drops its pick-a-look step, Magic Patterns launches MagicOS, Chrome iterates on HTML-in-Canvas. What it means for your workflow.
- [Tutorial: have an agent build a landing page using UI Hub as context](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/tutorial-agent-builds-landing-with-ui-hub/): Six steps from an empty folder to a verified page: load AGENTS.md, search the encyclopedia, pick components, load skills, build, verify in a browser.
- [Claude Design everywhere: out of beta, into every chat](https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/blog/claude-design-everywhere/): Anthropic took Docs, Slides and Design out of beta on every plan, launched Dashboards and Motion in beta, and will close the standalone Design site on 14 Dec 2026. For UI builders the practical move is to migrate the design system now.

## Top component libraries
- [Radix Primitives](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives): 无样式、可访问的 React 底层组件：对话框、下拉菜单、选择器、Tabs、Tooltip 等，shadcn/ui 的地基
- [Radix Themes](https://www.radix-ui.com/themes): Radix 官方带样式组件主题，开箱即用、配色体系完整
- [Headless UI](https://headlessui.com/): Tailwind 团队出品的无样式组件：弹窗、菜单、列表框、开关、Tabs
- [Ark UI](https://ark-ui.com/): Chakra 团队的无样式组件，45+ 组件，React / Vue / Solid / Svelte 通用
- [Park UI](https://park-ui.com/): 基于 Ark UI 的带样式组件，Panda CSS / Tailwind 两套写法
- [shadcn/ui Blocks](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks): shadcn 官方区块：登录页、侧边栏、仪表盘、日历，可直接用 CLI 添加
- [shadcn/ui Charts](https://ui.shadcn.com/charts): shadcn 官方图表：面积、柱状、折线、饼图、雷达，基于 Recharts
- [shadcn Registry 目录](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/directory): shadcn 官方收录的第三方组件注册表目录，一站找到各家兼容 shadcn 的组件
- [daisyUI](https://daisyui.com/): 最流行的 Tailwind 组件类名插件，60+ 组件、30+ 主题
- [Flowbite](https://flowbite.com/): Tailwind 组件库，开源版 50+ 组件；原站另有付费 Pro 区块
- [HyperUI](https://www.hyperui.dev/): 免费 Tailwind 组件片段合集：营销页、电商、后台，复制即用
- [Preline UI](https://preline.co/): Tailwind 组件与区块，开源部分免费；原站另有付费 Pro
- [Meraki UI](https://merakiui.com/): Tailwind 组件，支持 RTL 和暗色模式
- [Tailwind Plus](https://tailwindcss.com/plus): Tailwind 官方付费组件与模板（原 Tailwind UI），500+ 组件；本站只放链接
- [Mantine](https://mantine.dev/): 100+ 组件和 70+ hooks，自带日期、图表、富文本、通知
- [Chakra UI](https://chakra-ui.com/): 老牌 React 组件库，主题系统灵活，v3 基于 Ark UI
- [MUI Material UI](https://mui.com/material-ui/): Material Design 的 React 实现，组件最全之一
- [MUI X](https://mui.com/x/): 数据表格、日期选择、图表、树视图；基础版免费开源，Pro / Premium 付费
- [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/): Radix / MUI / Floating UI 作者合作的无样式组件库
- [React Aria](https://react-aria.adobe.com/): Adobe 出品，无障碍做得最细的无样式组件与 hooks
- [Ant Design](https://ant.design/): 蚂蚁中后台组件库，60+ 组件，表格表单极强
- [Ant Design Mobile](https://mobile.ant.design/): 蚂蚁移动端组件库
- [AntV G2](https://g2.antv.antgroup.com/): 蚂蚁可视化语法，几十种图表
- [TDesign](https://tdesign.tencent.com/): 腾讯企业级设计体系，React / Vue / 小程序 / 移动端全覆盖
- [Arco Design](https://arco.design/): 字节中后台组件库，60+ 组件，带物料市场
- [Semi Design](https://semi.design/): 抖音前端出品，设计到代码一体，组件细节好
- [Naive UI](https://www.naiveui.com/): Vue 3 组件库，90+ 组件，主题可调
- [Element Plus](https://element-plus.org/): 饿了么 Vue 3 组件库，国内后台最常用
- [Vuetify](https://vuetifyjs.com/): Vue 的 Material 组件框架
- [PrimeVue](https://primevue.org/): Vue 组件库，90+ 组件；原站另有付费模板
- [PrimeReact](https://primereact.org/): React 版 Prime 组件库，90+ 组件；原站另有付费模板
- [PrimeNG](https://primeng.org/): Angular 版 Prime 组件库；原站另有付费模板
- [Nuxt UI](https://ui.nuxt.com/): Nuxt 官方组件库，基于 Reka UI + Tailwind
- [Reka UI](https://reka-ui.com/): Vue 版 Radix（原 Radix Vue），无样式可访问组件
- [shadcn-vue](https://www.shadcn-vue.com/): shadcn/ui 的 Vue 移植
- [Quasar](https://quasar.dev/): Vue 全家桶框架，一套代码出网页 / 移动 / 桌面
- [Vant](https://vant-ui.github.io/vant/): 有赞移动端 Vue 组件库
- [shadcn-svelte](https://www.shadcn-svelte.com/): shadcn/ui 的 Svelte 移植
- [Bits UI](https://bits-ui.com/): Svelte 无样式组件

- [Kobalte](https://kobalte.dev/): SolidJS 无样式可访问组件
- [Angular Material](https://material.angular.dev/): Angular 官方 Material 组件
- [Spartan](https://www.spartan.ng/): Angular 版 shadcn 风格组件
- [NG-ZORRO](https://ng.ant.design/): Ant Design 的 Angular 实现
- [Fluent UI](https://react.fluentui.dev/): 微软 Fluent 2 设计体系的 React 组件
- [Carbon Design System](https://carbondesignsystem.com/): IBM 设计体系，数据密集型界面优秀
- [Primer](https://primer.style/): GitHub 设计体系的 React 组件

- [Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com/): 经典 CSS 组件框架
- [Bulma](https://bulma.io/): 纯 CSS 组件框架，无 JS
- [Pico CSS](https://picocss.com/): 极简语义化 CSS，HTML 写完就好看
- [Open Props](https://open-props.style/): CSS 变量设计令牌：颜色、阴影、渐变、缓动
- [Tremor](https://tremor.so/): 仪表盘组件和图表，Tailwind + Recharts

## FAQ
- **What is UI Hub?** A free, curated directory of 2391 public UI resources: 134 component libraries, 1924 component style demos with light/dark screenshots, 68 design skills for AI agents, plus effects, templates, specs and tutorials. It links to original sites and never hosts paid source code.
- **How do I find a component in a given style?** Load https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/api/resources.json and filter by ct (component kind, e.g. "dialog") and vs (visual style, e.g. "minimal" or "motion"). type="style" entries are concrete component demos with a libName and page URL; type="library" entries are whole libraries with install info on the site.
- **Which skills should an agent use for good UI?** One direction skill (frontend-design or taste-skill), emil-design-eng for motion and interaction polish, then impeccable, baseline-ui, web-design-guidelines and accessibility as an audit pass. See https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/api/skills.json.
- **Can I copy the code?** Open-source libraries can be used under their own licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0 etc.); the card shows the original link. Paid tiers (marked paid/freemium) must be bought from the original vendor.
- **How often is it updated?** Daily via a GitHub Actions job that adds new UI repositories and tools from GitHub, awesome-shadcn-ui and Hacker News. Nothing is deleted. Last update: 2026-10-15 04:35 UTC.


# Blog posts (full text, English)

## AI-assisted UI design: a workflow that keeps taste in the loop

Every AI UI generator converges on the statistical middle of its training data: centred hero, three feature cards, a purple gradient. That is not a bug, it is what "most likely next token" means. The practical consequence is that speed is free and taste is the scarce input.
Split the job into four passes
Direction (human). Write a one-paragraph brief: audience, one adjective you want and one you refuse, a reference product, density level. NN/g's testing of AI design tools found outputs were generic unless the prompt carried real context.
Exploration (AI). Ask v0 or Claude for 4–6 deliberately different directions, not one "best" page. Diversity is where generators shine.
Curation (human). Pick one, then name what is wrong in concrete terms: "line length over 80ch", "two accent colours competing".
Polish (AI + human). Feed those notes back, or run a critique skill such as impeccable or baseline-ui, then do the last 10% by hand.
Our take
The biggest win is not generation but constraint files: a short DESIGN.md with tokens, spacing scale and banned patterns that every agent reads first. It turns one good decision into a hundred consistent screens. On UI Hub, filter by Skill to find ready-made ones.
ChecklistBrief has a "never" listAsk for variants, not a pageCritique with named problemsLock decisions into tokens

References:
- Status Update: AI UX-Design Tools Are Not Ready for Primetime — Nielsen Norman Group: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ai-design-tools-not-ready/
- v0 Documentation — Vercel: https://v0.app/docs
- Agent Skills repository — Anthropic: https://github.com/anthropics/skills
- impeccable — Paul Bakaus: https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable

## Prompting for UI: write specs, not wishes

A UI prompt is a tiny design spec. The model fills every gap with defaults, so each gap you leave becomes a cliché.
The six-slot template
Goal: pricing page for a dev tool, 3 tiers, annual toggle
Layout: 12-col, max 1200px, tiers in a row ≥ 900px, stacked below
Tokens: Geist, 14/20 body, radius 10, one accent #2563eb, neutral greys
States: hover, focus-visible ring, selected tier, loading on CTA
Content: real copy below (no lorem), prices 0 / 19 / 49
Avoid: gradients on text, glassmorphism, emoji icons, centred everything
Why it works
Vercel's design guidelines and Rauno Freiberg's "Interfaces" both stress small, checkable rules: focus states, hit targets, tabular numbers. Turning those into explicit lines makes the output verifiable. Real content matters too; placeholder text hides overflow and hierarchy problems.
Our takePut the "Avoid" line first when iterating. Models obey negative constraints better once they have seen the bad version. Keep a reusable prompt per component type; UI Hub's component cards include a copyable prompt you can start from.

References:
- Web Interface Guidelines — Vercel: https://vercel.com/design/guidelines
- Web Interface Guidelines (interfaces.rauno.me) — Rauno Freiberg: https://interfaces.rauno.me
- v0 Documentation — Vercel: https://v0.app/docs
- Refactoring UI — Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger: https://www.refactoringui.com

## Design-to-code with AI: map to your components, not to pixels

Early design-to-code tools translated frames into absolutely positioned divs. They looked right and were unmaintainable. The current generation, Figma's Dev Mode MCP server and Builder.io's Visual Copilot among them, works differently: it reads structure and variables and maps them to code you already own.
What to feed the agentTokens exported as CSS variables, so colours map to var(--accent) instead of hex.A component registry, for example a shadcn registry, so "button" means your Button.Auto-layout in the file. Frames without it force the model to guess flex rules.
Our takeTreat generated code as a pull request from a junior: correct-looking, missing edge states. Always check empty, loading, error and long-text states, and run an a11y pass. Teams that publish a registry once get compounding returns from every later generation.

References:
- Introducing the Figma MCP server — Figma: https://www.figma.com/blog/introducing-figma-mcp-server/
- Figma to code with Visual Copilot — Builder.io: https://www.builder.io/blog/figma-to-code-visual-copilot
- shadcn/ui Registry — shadcn: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry
- Tailwind CSS dark mode docs — Tailwind Labs: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/dark-mode

## Teaching agents taste: how design skills de-slop AI interfaces

An agent skill is a folder with a SKILL.md the agent reads when the task matches its description. For design, that means opinions survive between sessions instead of living in one long prompt.
A working stackDirection: frontend-design or taste-skill before writing code. They push a committed aesthetic and ban the usual tells.Craft: emil-design-eng for motion and micro-interaction judgement.Audit: impeccable, baseline-ui and web-design-guidelines after a draft exists.Redesign: redesign-skill when upgrading an existing site.
Our takeDo not load everything at once. Overlapping skills give conflicting advice. Use one direction skill, one craft skill and one audit skill per task. Write project-specific "never" rules in AGENTS.md so they override generic taste.

References:
- Agent Skills repository — Anthropic: https://github.com/anthropics/skills
- taste-skill — Leonxlnx: https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill
- impeccable — Paul Bakaus: https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable
- AGENTS.md — agents.md: https://agents.md
- Web Interface Guidelines — Vercel: https://vercel.com/design/guidelines

## Component composition: why headless + copy-paste won

The old model was a styled npm package you fought with overrides. shadcn/ui flipped it: behaviour and accessibility from Radix primitives, styling in Tailwind, and the source copied into your repo.
Why it suits AICode in your repo is visible context, so the agent can read and edit it.Compound components (&lt;Dialog.Trigger&gt;, &lt;Dialog.Content&gt;) have small, predictable surfaces, which makes edits less error-prone than a 40-prop monolith.Registries let tools install the same component into any project.
Our takeCompose from three layers: primitives (Radix, Ark, React Aria), your styled kit, and page blocks. Let AI work mainly at the block layer and keep primitives untouched. Atomic design's old atoms→organisms idea maps neatly onto this.

References:
- shadcn/ui docs — shadcn: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs
- Radix Primitives introduction — WorkOS / Radix: https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/overview/introduction
- Compound Pattern — patterns.dev (Lydia Hallie & Addy Osmani): https://www.patterns.dev/react/compound-pattern/
- Atomic Design, chapter 2 — Brad Frost: https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/chapter-2/

## Motion that feels right: purpose, duration, easing, restraint

Emil Kowalski's rule of thumb is blunt: if a user triggers something a hundred times a day, do not animate it. Motion is for orientation (where did this come from?), feedback (it worked) and, sparingly, delight.
Numbers to start fromSmall UI changes: 150–250ms; larger surfaces 300–400ms. Material 3's motion tokens sit in the same ranges.Enter with ease-out, so the element responds immediately; avoid ease-in for UI.Animate transform and opacity only for smooth 60fps.Respect prefers-reduced-motion: swap movement for fades.
Our takeAceternity- and Magic UI-style effects (beams, spotlights, marquees) work as one hero moment per page. Stack three and the page looks like a template. Josh Comeau's transition guide is the best explanation of why easing curves matter.

References:
- Great animations — Emil Kowalski: https://emilkowal.ski/ui/great-animations
- animations.dev — Emil Kowalski: https://animations.dev
- Motion overview — Material 3 — Google: https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview
- An Interactive Guide to CSS Transitions — Josh W. Comeau: https://www.joshwcomeau.com/animation/css-transitions/
- prefers-reduced-motion — MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion
- Motion docs — Motion: https://motion.dev/docs

## Dark mode done right: tokens, elevation and contrast

Inverting colours gives you pure black backgrounds, glowing saturated blues and shadows nobody can see. Apple's HIG and web.dev both describe dark mode as its own design pass.
RulesSemantic tokens: --bg, --surface, --ink, --accent, swapped per theme with [data-theme] or prefers-color-scheme.Elevation by lightness: raised surfaces get slightly lighter, because shadows barely read on dark.Off-black, off-white: e.g. #06070b and #f3f5fb reduce halation.Desaturate accents and re-check 4.5:1 text contrast in both themes.Set color-scheme so form controls and scrollbars follow.
Our takeNN/g's research shows preference is split, so ship both and remember the choice. Screenshots of previews need both themes too; UI Hub stores light and dark shots per component for exactly this reason.

References:
- Dark Mode — Human Interface Guidelines — Apple: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode
- prefers-color-scheme: Hello darkness, my old friend — web.dev (Thomas Steiner): https://web.dev/articles/prefers-color-scheme
- Dark Mode vs. Light Mode: Which Is Better? — Nielsen Norman Group: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode/
- Dark mode — Tailwind CSS: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/dark-mode

## Accessibility in AI-generated UI: the checks models skip

Models optimise for what a screenshot shows. Focus order, accessible names and live regions do not show up in screenshots, so they are the first things to go missing.
The checks models skip mostClickable divs instead of &lt;button&gt;. Prompt for semantic elements explicitly.Missing focus-visible styles, often removed with outline:none.Icon-only buttons without aria-label.Contrast of grey-on-grey secondary text (WCAG 1.4.3).Target size: at least 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8).Dialogs without focus trap and Escape. Use the ARIA APG patterns or Radix and React Aria.
Our takeMake accessibility structural, not a final pass. Generate on top of accessible primitives and add an audit skill (accessibility, web-design-guidelines) to the agent's definition of done.

References:
- Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 — W3C: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
- ARIA Authoring Practices Guide — W3C WAI: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/
- Radix Primitives introduction — Radix: https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/overview/introduction
- Web Interface Guidelines — Vercel: https://vercel.com/design/guidelines

## v0 in practice: from a prompt to shadcn code you can keep

v0 by Vercel generates React components built on shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS. That stack choice is the whole point: the output is ordinary, readable code using primitives many teams already ship, so the result can leave the tool. Treat v0 as a fast pair-programmer for UI, and judge it by whether you would merge its code.
A brief that works
Name the components. "Use Card, Tabs and a Table with a sticky header" beats "make a nice dashboard". v0 knows the shadcn vocabulary, so use it.
Give tokens, not adjectives. Radius, one accent colour, font, density. "Modern" means nothing to a model; --radius: 0.5rem does.
List the states. Empty, loading, error, long text. Generators default to the happy path.
Paste real content. Lorem ipsum hides layout bugs; real names and prices expose them.
Iterate in small, named steps
Ask for one change per turn ("tighten the table to 40px rows; keep everything else"). Big rewrites tend to regress parts you already liked. When something is right, say so explicitly so it stays.
Getting the code out
v0 lets you add generated code to a project through the shadcn CLI or download it, and it deploys to Vercel. Whichever path you take, review it like a PR: check that colours come from CSS variables rather than hard-coded hex, that interactive elements are real buttons and links, and that focus styles exist.
Our take
v0's ceiling is your brief and your design system. Teams that already use shadcn get the most out of it because the output drops straight into their codebase. Pair it with a taste skill or the guidelines in our encyclopedia to avoid the generic "centred hero + three cards" result.

References:
- v0 by Vercel — Vercel: https://v0.app/
- v0 documentation — Vercel: https://v0.app/docs
- shadcn/ui — shadcn: https://ui.shadcn.com/
- shadcn CLI docs — shadcn: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli

## Lovable and Bolt: when prompt-to-UI becomes prompt-to-app

Lovable and Bolt (by StackBlitz) sit one step beyond component generators: you describe an app and they scaffold front end, routing and, through integrations such as Supabase, a backend. Bolt runs the dev environment in the browser on StackBlitz's WebContainers. The design question changes accordingly: the model is juggling schema, auth and deploys, so visual decisions get made by default unless you make them first.
A notable change this month
On 8 October 2026 Lovable's changelog removed the three "design directions" it used to show before the first build of a visually open-ended prompt. It now derives the look from your description and asks about colour, typography and layout only when the prompt leaves them open. In practice: your prompt is now the art brief. If you don't write one, you get the default.
Front-load the look
Open with a style paragraph before any feature list: palette, type, radius, density, one reference site.
Ask for a static UI pass first, with fake data, and approve it before wiring the backend.
Keep a design.md or similar guideline file in the project and tell the tool to follow it on every change.
After each feature, check the new screens against that file; drift creeps in one screen at a time.
When to pick which
Use these tools when you need a working prototype with real data paths fast. Use a component generator (v0, Magic Patterns) or hand-built code when the deliverable is a polished interface inside an existing codebase. Many teams do both: prototype the flow in an app builder, rebuild the final UI with their own system.

References:
- Lovable changelog (8 Oct 2026) — Lovable: https://docs.lovable.dev/changelog
- Lovable cut its pick-a-look step — Art Direction Daily: https://artdirectiondaily.com/issues/2026-10-12-lovable-cut-pick-look-step.html
- Bolt.new — StackBlitz: https://bolt.cello.so/ByQ3siiRkMz
- WebContainers — StackBlitz: https://webcontainers.io/
- Lovable Supabase integration — Lovable: https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase

## Figma Make and the Figma agent: AI moves onto the canvas

Figma Make, introduced at Config 2025, generates interactive prototypes and simple apps from a prompt, and can start from an existing Figma frame. It answered the question designers kept asking about v0-style tools: "can I do this where my designs already live?"
The agent goes GA
On 6 October 2026 Figma made its product-design agent generally available, after a beta that began in May. Two additions stand out in the coverage: library owners can supply guidelines (markdown files) that the agent reads whenever that library is enabled, and teammates can watch the agent's activity live on the canvas.
Why the guideline file is the real feature
It moves art direction from a per-session prompt into a file the team maintains and reviews.
It makes AI output consistent across people, not just across one person's sessions.
It is the same pattern as SKILL.md, Cursor rules and Lovable project knowledge: durable, versioned design context.
What to put in yours
Token names and when to use each; spacing and type scales; component do/don't pairs; voice and tone for UI copy; a short "never" list (no text gradients, no emoji icons, no centred body text). Keep it short enough that a reviewer actually reads it, and link to examples rather than describing them. Our encyclopedia's spec digests are a reasonable starting template.

References:
- Figma Make — Figma: https://www.figma.com/make/
- Figma's AI agent for product design is now generally available — The Verge: https://www.theverge.com/tech/1004953/figmas-ai-agent-for-product-design-is-now-generally-available
- Figma release notes — Figma: https://www.figma.com/release-notes/
- Lovable cut its pick-a-look step (Figma section) — Art Direction Daily: https://artdirectiondaily.com/issues/2026-10-12-lovable-cut-pick-look-step.html

## MagicOS: Magic Patterns bets on an infinite canvas of AI threads

Magic Patterns started as a prompt-to-UI tool aimed at product teams (it launched on Hacker News as YC W23, intentionally front-end only). On 13 October 2026 it introduced MagicOS, which reorganises the product around an infinite canvas rather than one chat and one preview.
How it is structured
Canvas: everything is a file on it: designs, documents, images, GitHub repos, notes.
Coordinator: the chat you talk to. It answers small questions and turns real work into threads.
Threads: each is an agent doing one piece of work; they run in parallel and report back.
Sidebar: threads by status, so you see what is waiting on you.
What problem it targets
Anyone who has explored five directions in five chat tabs knows the pain: you repeat the brief in each, lose rejected options, and forget why you picked one. MagicOS keeps PRDs, references, variants and rejected directions side by side, and the coordinator reads the canvas so you explain less. It also offers real-time voice and an MCP server so Claude, Cursor or Codex can build from what is on the canvas.
When not to use it
Magic Patterns' own docs say a single design still fits better for one page or a quick prototype, and that some features (Plan Mode, Controls, forking, merging, inline comments) were single-design only at launch. Our take: use the canvas for exploration-heavy work, keep the single design for focused polish.

References:
- Introducing MagicOS — Magic Patterns: https://www.magicpatterns.com/blog/introducing-magicos
- What is MagicOS — Magic Patterns docs: https://www.magicpatterns.com/docs/documentation/magic-os/overview
- MagicOS vs. Designs — Magic Patterns docs: https://www.magicpatterns.com/docs/documentation/magic-os/when-to-use-magicos
- Launch HN: Magic Patterns (YC W23) — Hacker News: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43752176

## Prompt-to-UI tools compared: v0, Lovable, Bolt, Figma Make, Magic Patterns

All five tools turn words into interface, but they are built for different jobs. Comparing them on "which looks best" is unreliable because output depends mostly on your prompt. Compare them on what they produce and where it goes.
By deliverable
Components for an existing React codebase: v0 (shadcn/Tailwind output, CLI install).
A working full-stack prototype: Lovable or Bolt (backend integrations, in-browser dev env for Bolt).
Prototypes next to your design files: Figma Make; the Figma agent for edits on the canvas with team guidelines.
Product-team exploration across many directions: Magic Patterns, now with the MagicOS canvas and an MCP server for coding agents.
Questions that decide it
Will engineers keep the code, or is this throwaway?
Do you need to match an existing design system? (Check whether the tool can import components or guideline files.)
Who iterates: a designer on a canvas, or a developer in a repo?
Where does the design context live, and can every teammate's session read it?
Our take
The 2026 trend across all five is the same: durable context (guideline files, design systems, MCP) beats clever prompting. Pick the tool whose context mechanism fits your team, and invest in that file. Pricing and limits change often, so check each vendor's current page rather than any comparison table, including ours.

References:
- v0 — Vercel: https://v0.app/
- Lovable docs — Lovable: https://docs.lovable.dev/
- Bolt.new — StackBlitz: https://bolt.cello.so/ByQ3siiRkMz
- Figma Make — Figma: https://www.figma.com/make/
- Magic Patterns — Magic Patterns: https://www.magicpatterns.com/

## Aceternity UI deep dive: spectacle, used sparingly

Aceternity UI, created by Manu Arora, is a collection of copy-paste components built with React, Tailwind CSS and Motion (formerly Framer Motion). It is known for showpiece effects: spotlight and beam backgrounds, 3D cards, animated grids, parallax hero scrolls. Free components are open to copy; there is also a paid tier of templates and blocks.
What works on real pages
One ambient background behind the hero (grid, dots, a soft spotlight). It adds depth without competing with copy.
Bento grids and feature sections with restrained hover motion.
Text reveal or typewriter for a single headline, not for paragraphs.
What to avoid
Stacking three effects in one viewport, animating body text, and 3D tilt on cards that hold data. These read as a demo reel and cost performance on low-end phones. Always respect prefers-reduced-motion, which several effects do not handle by default, so wrap them yourself.
How we use it in UI Hub
Aceternity is one of the references behind the user's "restrained fancy" house style: borrow one signature effect per page, keep typography and spacing doing the heavy lifting. Search "aceternity" in the hub to see every Aceternity component we index with a live preview.

References:
- Aceternity UI — Manu Arora: https://ui.aceternity.com/
- Aceternity UI components — Aceternity: https://ui.aceternity.com/components
- Motion for React — Motion: https://motion.dev/
- prefers-reduced-motion — MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion

## Magic UI deep dive: animated components that install like shadcn

Magic UI is an open-source library of animated components (MIT licence) designed as a companion to shadcn/ui. Components are added with the shadcn CLI from Magic UI's registry, so the source lands in your repo where you can edit it, rather than living in a dependency.
Picks that earn their place
Marquee for logo walls and testimonials: motion that carries information.
Number ticker for a single headline metric.
Animated beam / orbiting circles to show integrations, one per page.
Shimmer or border-beam buttons for exactly one primary CTA.
Accessibility and performance
Continuous motion (marquees, orbits) should pause on hover and stop under prefers-reduced-motion; WCAG 2.2.2 asks for a way to pause anything that moves for more than five seconds. Prefer transform and opacity animations, which browsers can composite cheaply.
Our take
Magic UI is the easiest way to add motion to a shadcn project because it shares the install model and the token variables. The risk is the same as any effects library: use one or two components per page, and let the rest of the UI stay calm.

References:
- Magic UI — Magic UI: https://magicui.design/
- magicuidesign/magicui (MIT) — GitHub: https://github.com/magicuidesign/magicui
- Understanding SC 2.2.2: Pause, Stop, Hide — W3C: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html
- shadcn registry docs — shadcn: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry

## Cult UI deep dive: tactile components with personality

Cult UI is an open-source collection of shadcn-compatible components with a distinctly tactile feel: a dynamic-island style container, textured and "neumorphic-lite" buttons, expandable cards, and playful toolbars. Where Aceternity leans on spectacle, Cult UI leans on interaction feel: springs, squish and layout animation.
Where it shines
Small product surfaces (toolbars, popovers, status pills) that benefit from springy layout transitions.
Portfolio and indie-product pages where personality is the point.
Learning material: reading the source is a good way to learn layout animation with Motion.
Keeping consistency
Personality components drift from your system fast. Before adopting one, map its colours and radii onto your tokens, match its spring settings across components so motion feels like one family, and check keyboard support: custom toggles and islands need visible focus and proper roles.
Our take
Cult UI is a reference for the "Cult" in the house style list: tactile micro-interaction over loud backgrounds. Pick one signature interaction per product and let it recur, rather than mixing every clever component on one page.

References:
- Cult UI — Cult UI: https://www.cult-ui.com/
- nolly-studio/cult-ui — GitHub: https://github.com/nolly-studio/cult-ui
- Layout animations — Motion: https://motion.dev/docs/react-layout-animations
- ARIA Authoring Practices Guide — W3C: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/

## shadcn blocks and registries: page sections as source code

shadcn/ui is not a package you install; it is a set of components whose source you copy into your project. Blocks extend the idea to whole sections: dashboards, sidebars, login and signup pages, charts. Each is added with the CLI, for example npx shadcn@latest add dashboard-01, and lands as editable files.
Registries: everyone can publish
The shadcn registry format lets any team publish components, blocks, hooks and theme files as JSON that the CLI understands. Magic UI, Cult UI and many others distribute this way, and you can run a private registry for your own design system.
npx shadcn@latest add https://your-registry.example/r/pricing-01.json
Why agents love this model
The code is local, so an agent can read and edit it like any file.
Names are stable and documented, so prompts can reference them ("add sidebar-07").
Theme lives in CSS variables, so one token change restyles everything the agent generated.
Our take
If you want AI-generated UI to stay consistent, give the agent a registry, not a style adjective. Start from official blocks, restyle via tokens, and publish your modified versions to a private registry so every future session builds from your system.

References:
- Blocks — shadcn/ui: https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks
- Registry — shadcn/ui: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry
- CLI — shadcn/ui: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli
- Theming — shadcn/ui: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming

## Typography for AI-generated UI: the fastest way to look less generic

Ask any generator for a landing page and you will usually get one sans-serif at body, heading and caption sizes. Typography is the cheapest lever to move a page away from that default, and it is easy to specify precisely in a prompt.
Five rules to put in the brief
Use a modular scale. Pick a ratio (1.2 for dense apps, 1.25–1.333 for marketing) and name the steps as tokens.
Pair two typefaces with a job each. A display face for headlines (a serif such as Instrument Serif, or a tight grotesk) and a workhorse sans for UI.
Tighten large text. Negative letter-spacing (around −0.02em) on display sizes; leave body text at default.
Constrain line length. Roughly 45–75 characters for Latin body text; use max-width: 65ch.
Fluid sizes. clamp() for headlines so mobile does not inherit desktop sizes.
CJK needs its own settings
For Chinese and Japanese, use a slightly larger line-height (about 1.7), avoid negative tracking, and use word-break: keep-all or text-wrap: balance on headings so short phrases are not orphaned, the fix we applied to our own Japanese headings.
Our take
If you only change one thing in AI output, change the type scale and the display face. It is a two-line token edit with a visible payoff.

References:
- Practical Typography: line length — Matthew Butterick: https://practicaltypography.com/line-length.html
- text-wrap — MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-wrap
- clamp() — MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/clamp
- Utopia fluid type scale — Utopia: https://utopia.fyi/type/calculator/
- Requirements for Chinese Text Layout — W3C: https://www.w3.org/TR/clreq/

## OKLCH colour systems: palettes that survive dark mode

OKLCH is a CSS colour space (CSS Color Level 4) defined by lightness, chroma and hue. Its lightness channel tracks perceived brightness far better than HSL's, so a yellow and a blue at the same L actually look similarly light. Tailwind CSS v4 switched its default palette to OKLCH, and all modern browsers support oklch().
Building a scale
--brand-50:  oklch(97% 0.02 250);
--brand-500: oklch(62% 0.17 250);
--brand-900: oklch(30% 0.09 250);
Keep hue fixed, step lightness evenly, and reduce chroma at the extremes, where sRGB screens cannot display high chroma anyway.
Dark mode by lightness, not inversion
Surfaces: very low L (around 14–20%) with a hint of the brand hue instead of pure black.
Text: high L but not 100%, to reduce glare.
Accent: raise L and lower chroma slightly so it does not vibrate on dark backgrounds.
Re-check contrast: equal OKLCH lightness differences do not guarantee WCAG ratios, so test with a contrast checker.
Our take
Give agents colour tokens in OKLCH with light and dark values side by side. It makes "make it darker" or "add a success colour" a predictable edit instead of a guess.

References:
- oklch() — MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/oklch
- OKLCH in CSS: why we moved from RGB and HSL — Evil Martians: https://evilmartians.com/chronicles/oklch-in-css-why-quit-rgb-hsl
- OKLCH Color Picker — oklch.com: https://oklch.com/
- Tailwind CSS v4.0 — Tailwind Labs: https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4
- WebAIM Contrast Checker — WebAIM: https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/

## Landing page teardown: what Linear and Vercel get right

Linear's and Vercel's homepages are among the most imitated in software. Copying their gradients misses the point; what is worth copying is a set of decisions you can see by reading the pages carefully. Screenshots below were captured on 14 October 2026; both sites change often.
Decisions worth stealing
One sentence of positioning in the hero, large, with a short supporting line. No feature list above the fold.
The product is the hero image. Real UI (or a faithful render of it) instead of an illustration, so the visitor sees what they would use.
Restraint in colour. Mostly neutral surfaces; accent colour reserved for action and emphasis.
Proof straight after the promise: customer logos or concrete product capabilities right below the hero.
Sections with one idea each, each with a short heading and a visual that demonstrates it.
What not to copy
Their brand recognition: a minimal hero works when people already know the name; a new product may need a more explicit line.
Heavy custom motion and 3D renders that took dedicated teams; a static, sharp product shot beats a mediocre animation.
Checklist for your page
Can a stranger say what you sell after five seconds? Is the first image your actual product? Is there exactly one primary CTA? Does every section prove one claim? If yes, the gradient is optional.

References:
- Linear homepage — Linear: https://linear.app/
- Vercel homepage — Vercel: https://vercel.com/
- The 5-second test — Nielsen Norman Group: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/first-impressions-human-automaticity/
- Landing page design best practices — Nielsen Norman Group: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/homepage-design-principles/

## Dashboard patterns that hold up: from KPI strip to drill-down table

Ask a generator for an "analytics dashboard" and you will likely get a sidebar, four stat cards and a grid of charts of equal weight. It looks complete and answers nothing. A better structure follows the questions a user actually asks, in order.
Three layers
Is everything OK? A KPI strip of 3–5 numbers, each with the comparison period and a direction, not a sparkline zoo.
What changed? One primary time-series chart with a range selector, annotated where something happened.
Why? A sortable, filterable table that drills into detail. Tables are where people actually work.
Details generators skip
Tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) so numbers align.
Right-aligned numeric columns, left-aligned text.
Empty, loading (skeleton) and error states for every widget.
Units and time zone in labels; a "last updated" timestamp.
Colour used for status only, with a non-colour cue (icon or text) for colour-blind users.
Components to start from
shadcn's dashboard blocks and its charts (built on Recharts) give you the scaffolding; Tremor offers dashboard-focused React components. Specify the three layers in your prompt and you get a page people can use, not just screenshot.

References:
- Dashboard blocks — shadcn/ui: https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks
- Charts — shadcn/ui: https://ui.shadcn.com/charts
- Tremor — Tremor: https://tremor.so/
- Dashboards: making charts and graphs easier to understand — Nielsen Norman Group: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/dashboards-preattentive/
- font-variant-numeric — MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/font-variant-numeric

## Design tokens for agents: the file that makes AI output on-brand

Agents follow concrete values far more reliably than descriptions. A design token file turns "clean, premium, a bit playful" into numbers the agent can apply everywhere. The W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) publishes a vendor-neutral JSON format for this, supported by tools such as Style Dictionary and Tokens Studio.
A minimal structure
{
  "color": { "accent": { "$type": "color", "$value": "oklch(62% 0.17 250)" } },
  "radius": { "md": { "$type": "dimension", "$value": "10px" } },
  "space": { "4": { "$type": "dimension", "$value": "16px" } }
}
Three tiers of naming
Primitive: raw values (blue-500, space-4).
Semantic: intent (surface, text-muted, accent, danger). Agents should mostly use these.
Component: optional overrides (button-radius).
Handing it to an agent
Export tokens to CSS variables and commit them; tell the agent "never hard-code colours or spacing, use these variables".
Add a one-page usage note: which token for which job, plus three do/don't pairs.
Reference both from your AGENTS.md, Cursor rules or skill so every session loads them.
Verify: grep generated code for raw hex values as a cheap lint.
Our encyclopedia's colour, spacing and type spec digests are written to be pasted into exactly this kind of usage note.

References:
- Design Tokens Community Group — W3C: https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/
- Design Tokens Format Module — DTCG: https://www.designtokens.org/
- Style Dictionary — Style Dictionary: https://styledictionary.com/
- Tokens Studio — Tokens Studio: https://tokens.studio/

## Design skills for Claude and Cursor: SKILL.md, rules and AGENTS.md

Anthropic's Agent Skills are folders with a SKILL.md file: YAML front matter (a name and a description) followed by instructions, optionally with scripts and assets. The agent sees the descriptions and loads a skill's full body only when it is relevant. Cursor offers project rules in .cursor/rules, and many coding agents read an AGENTS.md at the repo root. Different files, same idea: durable, scoped instructions.
What makes a design skill work
A precise description, because it decides when the skill loads ("Use when building or restyling web UI").
Bans before wishes. Models respond well to a short list of things never to do (text gradients, emoji icons, centred paragraphs, more than one accent).
Concrete values: tokens, scales, a reference to the token file.
A verification step: "render in a browser at 390px and 1440px, light and dark, before saying done".
A template
---
name: house-ui
description: Use when creating or restyling any web page or component.
---
1. Load tokens from styles/tokens.css. Never hard-code colour/spacing.
2. Type: Instrument Serif display, Geist UI, scale 1.25.
3. Never: text gradients, emoji icons, glassmorphism stacks.
4. One signature effect per page (see /kb/ house style).
5. Verify in a browser: 390/1440px, light/dark, keyboard focus.
Where to find good ones
Anthropic's public skills repository includes a frontend-design skill; community skills such as taste-skill and impeccable focus on aesthetics. Our encyclopedia indexes the ones we use, with full text where the licence allows.

References:
- Agent Skills overview — Anthropic: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview
- anthropics/skills — GitHub: https://github.com/anthropics/skills
- Rules — Cursor docs: https://docs.cursor.com/context/rules
- AGENTS.md — agents.md: https://agents.md/
- taste-skill — GitHub: https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill

## Tutorial: have an agent build a landing page using UI Hub as context

UI Hub is built to be read by agents: a JSON API, a design encyclopedia with raw Markdown per entry, and an AGENTS.md. This walkthrough shows the loop we use ourselves. Paste the prompts into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any agent that can fetch URLs.
Six steps
Load the guide. "Read https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/AGENTS.md and follow it."
Search the encyclopedia for the house style and the specs you need: /kb/?q=house style, /kb/?q=typography.
Pick components from /api/resources.json, filtered by type and licence; prefer open-source libraries you can copy.
Load skills in order: a taste or frontend-design skill first, then accessibility and quality checks.
Build with tokens in CSS variables, one signature effect, real copy.
Verify in a browser at 390px and 1440px, light and dark, and fix what you see before reporting done.
A prompt you can copy
Use UI Hub as design context: read /AGENTS.md, search /kb/ for
"house style", "typography", "colour". Build a landing page for
[product] with shadcn + one Aceternity background. Tokens in CSS
variables, 10-language-ready copy, then screenshot 390/1440 light/dark.
Why this works
Each step replaces a vague instruction with a document the agent can read. The Agents guide has a one-click copy of this prompt in 10 languages, plus a downloadable skill bundle.

References:
- UI Hub AGENTS.md — UI Hub: https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/AGENTS.md
- UI Hub design encyclopedia — UI Hub: https://siinxu.github.io/ui-resource-hub/kb/
- AGENTS.md convention — agents.md: https://agents.md/
- anthropics/skills — GitHub: https://github.com/anthropics/skills

## Claude Design everywhere: out of beta, into every chat

On 8 October 2026 Anthropic published a product update that matters more for design-and-code workflows than the headline tools might suggest. Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion entered beta; Claude Docs, Slides and Design left beta and are available on every Claude plan, including Free. The same post says the standalone Claude Design site at claude.ai/design stays open only until 14 December 2026, after which design work lives inside ordinary Claude conversations, Claude Code and the Artifacts tab.
What actually shipped
Design in every chat. Anthropic’s product page and help centre describe Claude Design as an artifact template: describe a visual, get a canvas beside the conversation, then refine with chat, inline comments and on-canvas edits. It works in Claude Code via /design and /design-sync, and on mobile for viewing and editing (sharing settings stay on web/desktop).
Design systems travel with you. Systems can be imported from GitHub, design files or a local codebase. Teams that used the standalone site can click “Migrate team design systems” on the Artifacts page; Anthropic notes migrated systems may need a “Let Claude clean it up” pass.
Dashboards (beta, paid). Connect Redshift, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Databricks, Snowflake or Salesforce-style connectors, ask in plain language, and get a live dashboard. Each number exposes the query behind it and a refresh time; deeper analysis can be sent to tools such as Amplitude, Grafana, Hex, Mixpanel, Omni, Perplexity, PostHog or Sigma.
Motion (beta, Team/Enterprise). Claude writes code that animates your own text, charts, shapes and images into a short explainer you can edit and export as MP4. Anthropic states it does not use a video-generation model and does not invent footage or people.
Enterprise defaults. Docs, Slides and Design turn on by default on 15 October 2026 (except HIPAA-enabled orgs). Dashboards and Motion stay off until an admin enables them under Organization settings → Artifacts.
Why it matters for UI builders
The useful shift is not “another AI design toy”. It is that the brief, the design system and the coding agent share one conversation surface. A prototype can start next to a requirements thread, inherit components via /design-sync, and hand off to Claude Code without screenshot archaeology. Connectors listed on the product page (Adobe, Canva, Gamma, Lovable, Miro, Replit, Vercel, Wix and others) push the same artifact into the tools you already ship from.
Anthropic’s own announcement claims more than 45 million docs, decks and designs since those templates arrived in every conversation. Treat that as a usage signal, not a quality guarantee: the ceiling is still your tokens, your refuse-list and whether an admin locked a single approved system.
Our take
Migrate the design system before December, not the day the standalone URL dies. Enterprise teams should treat 15 October as the day Design becomes ambient for everyone who can open Claude—so lock publishing rights and a default system first, or you will get fast, on-brand-looking noise. Prefer Motion when the story is your own data and copy; reach for a dedicated video model when you need filmed scenes. Prefer Dashboards for exploratory questions where seeing the SQL builds trust; keep your BI stack for governed reporting.
Practical checklist
Open Artifacts → migrate team design systems; run the clean-up pass on each.
In Claude Code, run /design-sync against the repo that owns tokens and components.
Write a short house guideline (tokens, type scale, never-list) the same way you would for Figma’s agent or a SKILL.md—Claude Design still needs a file it can obey.
Enterprise admins: decide before 15 October whether Docs/Slides/Design should stay default-on; enable Dashboards/Motion only after data connectors are reviewed.
Export path: HTML / PDF / PPTX for stakeholders; hand off to Claude Code or a connector (v0, Vercel, Lovable, Replit…) when the next step is production UI.
Verify like any generated UI: real content, focus rings, light/dark, 390px and 1440px—not only the canvas preview.

References:
- Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude — Anthropic: https://claude.com/resources/articles/dashboards-and-motion
- Claude Design product page — Anthropic: https://claude.com/product/design
- Get started with Claude Design — Claude Help Center: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design
- Claude Design admin guide for Team and Enterprise — Claude Help Center: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604406-claude-design-admin-guide-for-team-and-enterprise-plans
- Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion: Anthropic’s new beta tools — Mad Robot: https://madrobot.blog/2026/10/08/claude-dashboards-motion-beta-docs-slides-design-free-plan/

# Design encyclopedia entries (specs + notes, full; skills: see raw URLs)

# Spacing & layout

> Use one 4/8-based scale, a max content width, and consistent gutters; spacing communicates grouping.

## Rules
- **One scale:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96 px. No one-off values like 13 or 22.
- **Proximity = grouping:** space inside a group < space between groups (e.g. 8 inside, 24 between).
- **Content width:** body text 60–75 characters; page container 1120–1320 px; side gutters 20 px mobile, 40 px desktop.
- **Grid:** 12 columns desktop, 4 columns mobile; align cards to the same edges as headings and filters.
- **Density:** tools and dashboards can be dense (row height 36–40 px); marketing pages breathe (section padding 64–120 px).
- **No dead space:** a card should not have a large empty middle; size containers to content or fill with real content.

## Tokens
```css
:root{--s1:4px;--s2:8px;--s3:12px;--s4:16px;--s5:24px;--s6:32px;--s7:48px;--s8:64px;--max:1320px;--gut:20px}
@media(min-width:900px){:root{--gut:40px}}
```

## Sources
- [Refactoring UI](https://www.refactoringui.com)
- [Apple HIG — Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout)
- [Laws of UX — Law of Proximity](https://lawsofux.com/law-of-proximity/)

# Typography

> Two families max, a modular type scale, tight display tracking, comfortable body leading, tabular numbers for data.

## Rules
- **Families:** one sans for UI (e.g. Geist, Inter), optionally one display serif (e.g. Instrument Serif) for headlines. Mono for code/data labels.
- **Scale:** 12 / 13 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64. UI body 14–16 px, line-height 1.5–1.65.
- **Display:** large headings line-height 1.0–1.15 and letter-spacing −0.01 to −0.02em.
- **Hierarchy with weight and colour, not only size:** secondary text uses a muted ink token, not a smaller font.
- **Numbers:** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for prices, tables, counters.
- **CJK:** add PingFang SC / Noto Sans CJK fallbacks; avoid letter-spacing on CJK body text.
- **Line length:** 60–75ch for reading text.

## Sources
- [Refactoring UI](https://www.refactoringui.com)
- [Web Interface Guidelines (Vercel)](https://vercel.com/design/guidelines)
- [Material 3 typography](https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/overview)

# Colour

> Neutral base + one accent; semantic tokens; check contrast in both themes; gradients only as accents.

## Rules
- **Palette:** a neutral ramp (bg, surface, mat, line, ink, ink2, ink3) + ONE accent + status colours (success/warn/danger).
- **Semantic tokens**, never raw hex in components: `--bg --surface --ink --ink2 --accent --line`.
- **Contrast:** text ≥ 4.5:1, large text and UI glyphs ≥ 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.3 / 1.4.11) in light AND dark.
- **Gradients:** restrained: a sheen on one headline word or a 1px border, not full rainbow backgrounds.
- **Avoid:** muddy mid-tones, two competing accents, saturated blue on pure black.

## Sources
- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
- [Material 3 colour](https://m3.material.io/styles/color/system/overview)
- [Tailwind CSS colours](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/colors)

# Motion

> Purposeful, fast (150–300 ms), ease-out on enter, transform/opacity only, honour reduced motion.

## Rules
- **Purpose:** orientation, feedback, continuity. Not decoration on frequent actions.
- **Durations:** micro 120–200 ms, panels 250–350 ms, page transitions ≤ 400 ms.
- **Easing:** ease-out (or spring with no overshoot) for enter; ease-in only for exits.
- **Performance:** animate `transform` and `opacity`; avoid animating layout properties.
- **Reduced motion:** `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` swaps movement for fades or nothing.
- **One hero effect per page** (beam, spotlight, marquee). Stacking effects looks like a template.

## Sources
- [Emil Kowalski — Great Animations](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/great-animations)
- [Material 3 motion](https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview)
- [MDN prefers-reduced-motion](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion)

# Accessibility

> Semantic HTML, visible focus, names for icon buttons, 24px targets, keyboard dialogs, WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Checklist
- Real `<button>`, `<a href>`, `<label>`; headings in order (one h1).
- `:focus-visible` ring on every interactive element; never bare `outline:none`.
- Icon-only buttons have `aria-label`; images have meaningful `alt` (or empty alt if decorative).
- Targets ≥ 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8); 44 px recommended on touch.
- Dialogs: focus trap, Esc to close, return focus. Prefer Radix / React Aria / APG patterns.
- Don't convey state by colour alone; announce async results via `aria-live`.
- Test: keyboard only, screen reader smoke test, 200% zoom, reduced motion.

## Sources
- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
- [ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [Radix Primitives](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/overview/introduction)

# Dark mode

> A second palette, not inversion: off-black base, elevation by lightness, desaturated accent, color-scheme set.

## Rules
- Swap semantic tokens with `[data-theme]` or `prefers-color-scheme`; remember the user's choice.
- Base off-black (#06070b–#121212), text off-white (#f3f5fb); avoid pure #000 / #fff pairs.
- Elevation by lighter surfaces; shadows barely read on dark.
- Desaturate / lighten the accent (e.g. #2563eb light → #67e8f9 dark) and re-check contrast.
- Set `color-scheme: light dark` so form controls and scrollbars follow.
- Previews and screenshots need both themes; never ship a "dark-only" demo without saying so.

## Sources
- [Apple HIG — Dark Mode](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode)
- [web.dev — prefers-color-scheme](https://web.dev/articles/prefers-color-scheme)
- [NN/g — Dark vs Light mode](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode/)

# Mobile & responsive

> Mobile-first layout, 44px touch targets, bottom navigation for primary tabs, safe areas, no horizontal scroll.

## Rules
- Design at 375 px first; breakpoints ~640 / 900 / 1280.
- Touch targets 44×44 px; spacing between targets ≥ 8 px.
- Primary navigation: bottom bar (3–5 items) on mobile; top tabs on desktop.
- Respect `env(safe-area-inset-*)` and use `viewport-fit=cover` only with padding.
- No horizontal scroll except intentional carousels with visible affordance.
- Inputs: 16 px font to avoid iOS zoom; correct `inputmode` / `enterkeyhint`.
- Test on a real device size in both themes.

## Sources
- [Apple HIG — Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout)
- [Material 3 — Navigation bar](https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-bar/overview)
- [WCAG 2.2 — Target Size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)

# House style: restrained fancy

> The UI Hub house style for sites we build: fancy but restrained, Aceternity / Magic UI / Cult UI quality, dense real content.

## The rule
"Fancy but restrained": polished like Aceternity UI, Magic UI and Cult UI, never loud.

## Do
- Information-dense cards: lead card + bento grid / collage, aligned edges, consistent gutters.
- One or two restrained accent colours; a gradient sheen on at most one word or edge.
- Real content in every cover and preview (real screenshots or meaningful diagrams).
- Refined motion: spotlight on hover, subtle entrance, ≤ 300 ms.
- Light + dark both designed; mobile checked at 375 px.
- 10 languages with automatic default by browser region.

## Don't (rejected in reviews)
- Documentation-site look for showcase pages.
- Big empty cards, blank covers, placeholder blocks, empty middles.
- Rainbow gradients and glow everywhere; glassmorphism as the main style.
- Muddy / dull palettes; misaligned columns; wrapped mid-word headings.

## Process
1. Read the UI Hub resources and skills first; pick a direction.
2. Produce ≥ 6 design options when the direction is open.
3. Build, then self-audit with impeccable / baseline-ui; deliver public link + light/dark screenshots.
4. If it is ugly, throw it away and redo rather than patching.

## References
- [Aceternity UI](https://ui.aceternity.com/components)
- [Magic UI](https://magicui.design/docs/components)
- [Cult UI](https://www.cult-ui.com)

# Lessons: previews and screenshots

> What we learned shipping 2,000+ component previews.

- Capture the actual component, not the marketing hero; crop to the component.
- Store light and dark shots; label "dark-only demo" honestly when the source has one theme.
- Never hotlink: save compressed WebP locally with credit to the original site.
- Re-check crops at card size: blurry or cut-off previews are worse than none.
- Thumbnails of whole sites are fine for "site" cards; component cards need component shots.


# Lessons: getting good UI from AI agents

> Practical rules that made agent-built UIs look designed instead of generated.

- Give the agent a short DESIGN brief with a "never" list before any code.
- Ask for several directions, choose one, then lock tokens.
- Load one direction skill, one craft skill, one audit skill; more causes conflicts.
- Require real copy; lorem ipsum hides hierarchy problems.
- Make the agent screenshot light/dark/mobile and look at them before saying "done".
